title: Week 1 Worklog
content:
Period: 05/10/2026 → 09/10/2026
Topic: Onboarding, AWS Account, Budgets, Support, IAM & VPC
Status: Planned
Week 1 Objectives: Meet and connect with FCAJ members, understand internship rules and regulations Create a secure AWS Free Tier account, master credit strategy and cost management with AWS Budgets Explore technical support offerings with AWS Support Plans and AWS Trusted Advisor Manage identity and access control with AWS IAM (User, Group, Policy, Role, MFA) Understand cloud networking fundamentals and deploy a custom Amazon VPC Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material Mon - Meet and connect with FCAJ members
- Read and review internship rules and company regulations 05/10/2026 05/10/2026 Tue - Create AWS Free Tier account:
+ Strategy to obtain full $200 credit and complete 5 earning tasks
+ List of credit killers to avoid unexpected costs
- Cost management with AWS Budgets:
+ Create Cost Budget & Usage Budget
+ Set up Billing Alerts sent to email 06/10/2026 06/10/2026 https://000001.awsstudygroup.com/ Wed - Explore AWS Support Plans:
+ Compare support tiers: Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise
+ Open Support Cases & inspect account health with AWS Trusted Advisor
- Access management with AWS IAM:
+ Core concepts: IAM User, IAM Group, IAM Policy
+ Hands-on: Create Admin Group & Admin User
+ Enable Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) 07/10/2026 07/10/2026 https://000002.awsstudygroup.com/ Thu - Advanced permissions with IAM Role & Switch Role:
+ Create IAM Role and OperatorUser
+ Practice Switch Role from OperatorUser to Admin Role
+ Enforce Principle of Least Privilege
- Networking fundamentals with Amazon VPC:
+ Concepts: VPC, CIDR block, Public Subnet vs Private Subnet
+ Route Table, Internet Gateway (IGW) & NAT Gateway
+ VPC Firewalls: Security Group (Stateful) vs Network ACLs (Stateless) 08/10/2026 08/10/2026 https://000003.awsstudygroup.com/ Fri - Hands-on deployment of Amazon VPC network:
+ Create Custom VPC with IPv4 CIDR Block
+ Create Public Subnet & Private Subnet
+ Create Internet Gateway (IGW) and attach to VPC
+ Configure Route Table routing traffic to Internet via IGW
+ Create Security Group allowing HTTP/SSH traffic
- Review Week 1 architecture: Account → Budgets → Support → IAM → VPC
- Clean up lab resources 09/10/2026 09/10/2026 https://000003.awsstudygroup.com/ Expected Week 1 Outcomes: Workplace Integration & Regulations: Successfully completed the onboarding process at First Cloud Journey (FCAJ); thoroughly understood company policies, information security standards, working schedules, and the overall internship training roadmap and deliverables. AWS Account Setup & Cost Governance: Successfully registered and activated a personal AWS account under the AWS Free Tier program. Mastered the strategy to acquire the full $200 AWS credit allowance and identified critical “credit killers” to proactively prevent unexpected cloud expenses. Established automated AWS Budgets (Cost & Usage Budgets) with 80% and 100% threshold notifications delivered via email alerts. Technical Support & Account Health Auditing: Understood the operational scope of AWS Support Plans (Basic, Developer, Business, Enterprise) and mastered submitting and managing Support Cases via AWS Support Center. Utilized AWS Trusted Advisor to assess account posture across core pillars: Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits. Identity and Access Management (AWS IAM): Mastered core IAM building blocks: Users, Groups, Policies, Roles, and permission boundary mechanisms. Implemented the Principle of Least Privilege by creating an Admin Group and non-root Admin User for daily operations, minimizing direct root account usage. Enforced Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) using virtual authenticator apps across both root and IAM user identities. Configured IAM Roles and executed Switch Role operations from OperatorUser to Admin Role, gaining hands-on insight into temporary security credentials. Cloud Networking Architecture (Amazon VPC): Acquired solid understanding of AWS networking concepts: IPv4 CIDR blocks, Public Subnets (Internet-facing), and Private Subnets (isolated workloads). Successfully architected and deployed a Custom VPC across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) for high availability. Attached an Internet Gateway (IGW) and configured Route Tables to properly direct outbound and inbound internet traffic. Differentiated and applied the two layers of VPC firewalls: Security Groups (Stateful host-level inspection) and Network ACLs (Stateless subnet-level filtering). Validated end-to-end network reachability, establishing a solid foundation for deploying compute and database resources in upcoming weeks.

title: Worklog
content:
The worklog records the AWS learning roadmap, studying Monday through Friday.

Week 2 (12/10–16/10): EC2, IAM Roles, S3 & RDS

title: Week 2 Worklog
content:
Period: 12/10/2026 → 16/10/2026
Topic: EC2, IAM Roles, S3 & RDS
Status: Planned
Week 2 Objectives: Master compute concepts and practice launching Amazon EC2 instances Configure secure connectivity to EC2 and deploy a sample web application Assign IAM Roles to EC2 to access AWS services securely without hardcoding Access Keys Store objects and host static websites using Amazon S3 Deploy Amazon RDS relational database in a Private Subnet and connect from EC2 Tasks to be carried out this week: Day Tasks Start Date Completion Date Reference Material Mon - Explore compute essentials with Amazon EC2:
+ Concepts: Instance types, AMI (Amazon Machine Image), EBS Volumes
+ Instance families (General Purpose, Compute, Memory Optimized)
- Hands-on EC2 deployment:
+ Launch EC2 Linux Instance (Amazon Linux 2023) in Public Subnet
+ Create and securely manage Key Pair (.pem)
+ Configure Security Group opening port 22 (SSH) and 80 (HTTP) 12/10/2026 12/10/2026 https://000004.awsstudygroup.com/ Tue - Connect and manage EC2 Instance:
+ Connect via SSH Client and EC2 Instance Connect
+ Manage EBS Volumes and create Snapshot backups
+ Create Custom AMI from running EC2 instance
- Deploy Web Application on EC2:
+ Install Web Server (LAMP stack / Node.js) on Amazon Linux 2023
+ Deploy sample AWS User Management application
+ Verify application access via Public IPv4 / Elastic IP 13/10/2026 13/10/2026 https://000004.awsstudygroup.com/ Wed - Authorize applications with IAM Roles for EC2:
+ Security risks of storing permanent Access Keys on compute instances
+ IAM Instance Profiles and temporary credential mechanisms
- Hands-on IAM Role for EC2:
+ Create S3 Bucket for storage
+ Create IAM Role with AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess permissions
+ Attach IAM Role to EC2 Instance
+ Verify S3 access via AWS CLI from EC2 without configuring access keys 14/10/2026 14/10/2026 https://000048.awsstudygroup.com/ Thu - Object storage with Amazon S3:
+ Concepts: S3 Bucket, Object, S3 URI, 11 9s durability (99.999999999%)
+ Object Versioning and Lifecycle Rules
- Hands-on Static Website Hosting on S3:
+ Create S3 Bucket and upload static website files (HTML, CSS, JS)
+ Enable Static Website Hosting
+ Configure Bucket Policy for Public Read and disable Block Public Access
+ Verify website access via S3 Website Endpoint 15/10/2026 15/10/2026 https://000057.awsstudygroup.com/ Fri - Relational Database with Amazon RDS:
+ Concepts: Amazon RDS and DB Engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB)
+ Multi-AZ architecture for high availability and Read Replicas
- Hands-on RDS deployment and connectivity:
+ Create DB Subnet Group across Private Subnets in VPC
+ Launch RDS MySQL Instance in Private Subnet
+ Configure Security Group allowing inbound traffic from EC2 on port 3306
+ Connect web application from EC2 to RDS database and verify data operations
- Clean up lab resources 16/10/2026 16/10/2026 https://000005.awsstudygroup.com/ Expected Week 2 Outcomes: Compute Foundations with Amazon EC2: Mastered EC2 hardware sizing metrics and instance families (General Purpose, Compute, Memory, Storage Optimized) to choose the optimal type for specific application workloads. Understood instance provisioning mechanisms using Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) and persistent block storage via Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS Volumes). Successfully launched an Amazon Linux 2023 EC2 instance within the Public Subnet of the custom VPC built in Week 1. Generated and securely managed SSH Key Pairs (.pem); configured inbound/outbound Security Group rules strictly limiting access to ports 22 (SSH) and 80 (HTTP). Remote Management & Application Deployment on EC2: Proficiently established remote management connections to EC2 instances using both standalone SSH clients and browser-based EC2 Instance Connect. Mastered EBS lifecycle management: volume attachment/detachment, live volume resizing, and taking point-in-time EBS Snapshots for data durability. Built custom AMIs from pre-configured running instances to establish standardized deployment images for future scaling. Successfully installed web server runtimes (LAMP stack / Node.js) on Amazon Linux 2023, deployed the AWS User Management sample application, and verified public accessibility via Elastic IP. Application Authorization via IAM Roles for EC2: Recognized severe security risks associated with embedding permanent Access Keys and Secret Access Keys in application code or server configuration files. Understood the underlying mechanisms of IAM Instance Profiles and the Instance Metadata Service (IMDSv2) for delivering short-lived temporary credentials. Created an IAM Role with least-privilege permissions (AmazonS3ReadOnlyAccess), attached it directly to the EC2 instance, and validated secure S3 data querying via the AWS CLI without permanent credentials. Object Storage & Static Website Hosting with Amazon S3: Mastered core S3 storage fundamentals: Buckets, Objects, S3 URIs, strong read-after-write consistency, and 11 9s of data durability (99.999999999%). Implemented advanced data governance features: enabled Object Versioning to prevent accidental deletion and configured Lifecycle Rules across S3 Storage Classes for cost efficiency. Successfully hosted a static web application on S3: uploaded website assets (HTML/CSS/JS), enabled Static Website Hosting, defined a Public Read Bucket Policy, adjusted Block Public Access settings, and tested global accessibility via the S3 Website Endpoint. Relational Database Management with Amazon RDS: Differentiated between self-managed databases hosted on EC2 versus AWS fully managed database services with Amazon RDS. Mastered Multi-AZ deployment concepts for automated synchronous failover and Read Replicas for scalable asynchronous read performance. Provisioned a dedicated DB Subnet Group across isolated Private Subnets, enforcing network isolation according to AWS Well-Architected security principles. Successfully launched an Amazon RDS MySQL/PostgreSQL instance; configured database Security Groups allowing inbound traffic on port 3306 strictly from the web EC2 Security Group. Connected the web tier application to the RDS database, verified CRUD database transactions, took a manual DB Snapshot, and executed a clean teardown of all provisioned cloud resources.
